newsitem.title: USA: Economic data to dictate start on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Economic data to dictate start on Wall Street.

text.p: U.S. stocks will take their lead at the start Tuesday from economic data, especially the first quarter Employment Cost Index, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.

With the focus having shifted back to the fate of interest rates and away from the quarter's mostly impressive earnings, the market will scrutinize every piece of wage or price related economic data for insight into what action the Federal Reserve will take on monetary policy when its policy-makers meet again on May 20.
"The reason the data are important is because the market makes them important," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
"We are on interest rate alert. This number will show us what has happened in terms of wages and growth in the first quarter. Everyone is guessing what the Fed will do."

He said the fact that the market managed to rally Monday despite sharp weakness in shares of Boeing Co was encouraging and suggested that the market "fundamentally feels that the economy is good and inflation is low."
The Tokyo stock market is closed Tuesday for a national holiday and will reopen Wednesday.
In London, the FTSE 100 was up 7.6 at 4397.3.

U.S. shares were moderately higher on Tuesday but trading volume was light as investors awaited the Employment Cost Index data. Boeing Co was up 3/8 at 95-5/8. PepsiCo Inc was up 1/8 at 31-3/8. International Business Machines Corp was up 1/4 at 150-5/8.
The dollar was weaker in Asia and stagnant above 1.73 marks and 126.50 yen in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were were slightly lower, with the long bond down 1/32 to yield 7.12 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that over the past 12 months, some of the best performance has come from managers who specialize in real estate securities -- though these weren't immune to the tremor that disturbed the market in March or April.

The New York Times Market Place writes that while small cap stocks have been badly trailing the larger market this year, some investors see opportunities in small issues with specialized niches and few significant competitors.
